title: Earthy Smoke Roasted Argentinian Pak Choi Gratin
description: A smoky, silky, and comforting side dish featuring pak choi, perfect for a lazy Sunday dinner. Inspired by the flavors of Argentina.

ingredients.name: Pak Choi
ingredients.notes: preferably with thick stems for best results

ingredients.name: Smoked Chorizo
ingredients.notes: choose a Spanish or Argentine brand for authentic flavor

ingredients.name: Smoked Paprika
ingredients.notes: or to taste, depending on smokiness desired

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: preferably flaky sea salt for best flavor

instructions: Carefully slice the pak choi in half lengthwise, cutting around the stems to preserve them.
Transfer the sliced pak choi to a large terracotta dish, cut side up, and set aside.
Heat the olive oil in a small saucepan over medium heat, then add the minced garlic and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute, stirring constantly to prevent burning.
Add the smoked chorizo to the saucepan and cook, breaking it up with a spoon, until it starts to brown and crisp slightly, about 3-4 minutes.
Sprinkle the smoked paprika over the pak choi in the terracotta dish, then pour the cooked chorizo and garlic mixture evenly over the top.
Season with salt and black pepper, then transfer the dish to the oven and roast for 15 minutes.
Top the roasted pak choi with heavy cream, then return to the oven and bake for an additional 5-7 minutes, or until the cream has slightly thickened and browned on top.
Remove from the oven and let cool slightly before serving, garnished with fresh herbs if desired.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh herbs and crusty bread on the side if desired.
Note: this recipe is for refrigerator pickling/preserving only — store in the refrigerator and consume within 1 week. Do not water-bath can without an acid (vinegar or lemon juice).
